The activity-label prompt with a leading `<system-reminder>` block is now recognized again. Your example text returns `True` from `is_activity_label_prompt`.

I couldn't run the test suite because pytest isn't installed here. The only check I ran was that one example.

**Root cause:** `strip_reminders()` in `anthrouter/request_text.py` is documented to "trim outer whitespace" but didn't. After the reminder block was removed, the newline that followed it stayed. `is_activity_label_prompt` then called `.startswith(ACTIVITY_LABEL_PREFIX)` on text that began with `\n`, so the match failed.

**Fix:** `strip_reminders()` now ends with `.strip()`, which is what its docstring already promised. I fixed it there rather than in `is_activity_label_prompt` so every caller gets the trimmed text. That includes the local-command matching in `handlers.py` and the classifier input in the model router.

I haven't checked whether any of those callers relied on the leftover whitespace, so run `make test` once pytest is available.
